taxonomic_note: Current Kew/POWO accepts Castilleja lindheimeri A.Gray and treats C. purpurea var. lindheimeri as a synonym.
look_here_first: Look at the colored bracts, not just the flowers. Lindheimer's paintbrush is a perennial hemiparasite with narrow leaves, upper leaves often lobed, and a terminal spike whose three-lobed bracts turn orange-red to scarlet around the much less conspicuous tubular flowers.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays — Purola Preserve natural flora under the older name C. purpurea var. lindheimeri. Travis — UT PRC herbarium index under the older varietal name. Williamson — detailed county treatment under the older varietal name. Current Kew taxonomy reconciles all three to accepted C. lindheimeri.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Historic source names are counted only after explicit synonym reconciliation. Joey's hemiparasitism discussion remains attributed field context.

best_field_traits: perennial hemiparasitic herb, several-stemmed from the base
leaves alternate, narrow linear to lanceolate
upper cauline leaves often divided into 2–3 narrow lobes
bract lobes orange-red to light scarlet
corolla strongly bilateral with beak-like upper lip
morphology_keys.hemiparasite_training: Green photosynthetic plant that also forms root connections to neighboring hosts; do not interpret a single nearby grass in a still frame as proof of the exact host individual.
morphology_keys.video_training: Joey labels the plant in thin Edwards Plateau limestone habitat and discusses hemiparasitic behavior.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Use perennial habit, narrow/lobed upper leaves, bract shape/color and flower structure together; the older C. purpurea var. lindheimeri name is the same learner concept.
